title: Render quad-layout patches in MeshNodeViewerScene with per-patch colors
description:
Surfaced during PATCH-42 housekeeping audit. The PATCH-37 quad-layout pipeline (cross-field -> seamless parametrization -> motorcycle graph -> T-mesh -> quantization) produces TPatch objects that the live MeshNodeViewerScene cannot currently render. This ticket wires the existing pipeline output into the existing renderer.

Pieces in place:
- MeshNodeViewerScene already renders procedural meshes
- PatchRenderer already supports per-face label -> color (used by the older MSC pipeline)
- TMesh.patches() returns 4-cycle TPatch objects with arc/corner ids
- Quantization.solve() returns integer arc lengths per patch

Pieces missing:
- QuadLayoutDecomposeNode: a MeshNode that wraps cross-field + IGM + tmesh + quantization and exposes per-face patch labels as a ScalarField
- Wiring from MeshNodeViewerScene to invoke that node and feed its output to PatchRenderer
- A test mesh that produces non-zero patches (cube produces 0 because every vertex is a singularity; Hand-30k currently produces 0 because IGM convergence isn't strong enough yet -- will need a torus or moderate-curvature mesh)

Blocker: T-mesh patch enumeration on real meshes. Currently only 4-cycles with no T-junctions are recognised. PATCH-44 (Lyon 2021 enhancements) will help with the proper arc-graph walk that produces meaningful patches at scale.

Out of scope:
- T-junction handling in patch enumeration (that's a separate ticket on TMesh.build)
- Coons-cage DSL emission (separate ticket)
- Upstream IGM convergence work
definition-of-done: On a moderate-curvature test mesh (sphere with non-trivial cross field, or torus) MeshNodeViewerScene displays the surface with each TPatch coloured by a unique RGB drawn from the existing golden-ratio-hue palette. Refresh time under 5s on a 1k-face mesh. Per-patch corners drawn as visible markers.
testing-plan: 1. Add a MeshNodeViewerSceneTest that loads a torus-2k mesh, runs the QuadLayoutDecomposeNode, and asserts patch_count > 0. 2. Visual: capture screenshot via ixdar-automation-cli, confirm distinct colours per patch. 3. Click on a patch -> overlay shows arc ids + quantization.
